note: A 20-acre block of bottomland timber on gravel Slater Avenue beside West Yellow Creek, north of Route E. MDC's one primitive camping spot is in the woods at the area's northeast corner: there is no parking lot, pad or drive, and a ditch runs between the road and the trees, so a motorhome has only the road edge. MDC's map marks Slater Avenue 'Impassable During Flood'. No facilities. --Claude
summary: MDC designates one primitive camping spot (map symbol, GIS 350 = pin) but it is in woods behind a roadside ditch with no lot, pad or drive anywhere on the 20 acres: more than a parking lot it is not - it is less. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written; kept with a caveat pending a keep/drop call. Phone matches.
flags: CRITERIA (keep-or-drop call for the owner; padless roadside): area page 'Things to Do: Camping: Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map' and 'Vehicle use is restricted to graveled and paved roads and established parking areas'; the map (Last Updated 10/10/2018) has one 'Primitive Camping' symbol in the NE corner beside Slater Ave and NO parking symbol; GIS 27 point 350; GIS 26 has no lot for this area. On 0.12 m/px leaf-off imagery the point is ~20 m inside continuous timber, west of gravel Slater Avenue, with a water-filled ditch between road and woods; no gravel pad, pull-off, lane or clearing is visible - only a ~15 m stub at the ditch's north end by the John Roth Rd junction. So the designation exists (not the lot rule: there is no lot at all) but nothing a vehicle can pull onto: a tent spot reached on foot from the road edge. Under 'padless roadside camping that MDC designates stays with a caveat' it stays, and the note carries the caveat; if the owner reads a ditch-separated woods spot with no place to leave the road as not drive-in, it is a drop. I read it as closer to a drop than the earlier padless cases.
ACCESS: the map prints 'Impassable During Flood' on Slater Avenue (the only road) - West Yellow Creek bottom; flood wording, no low-water crossing or 4WD wording. Gravel, 0.25 mile north of Route E.
PIN: stored 39.66017,-93.05177 = GIS 350, in woods. There is no lot to move it to; if kept, the nearest drivable point is the road edge at about 39.66020,-93.05150 (25 m E).

WATERFRONT: not waterfront kept. West Yellow Creek is on the area's west boundary ~400 m away; the impoundment north of the road junction is a private/levee wetland cell across a ditch, not in the camping spot's frontage.
PHONE: page '(660) 646-6122' matches stored (the brochure also names Grand Pass CA, 660/595-2444).
